--src: Mathlib.Order.Category.Preord
/-- The equivalence between `Preord` and itself induced by `OrderDual` both ways. -/
@[simps functor inverse]
def dualEquiv : Preord ≌ Preord where
  functor := dual
  inverse := dual
  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X
  counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X

--src: Mathlib.Order.Category.BddOrd

    BddOrd.dual ⋙ forget₂ BddOrd Bipointed =
    forget₂ BddOrd Bipointed ⋙ Bipointed.swap :=
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.Data.Num.Bitwise
@[simp] lemma lxor_eq_xor (p q : PosNum) : p.lxor q = p ^^^ q := rfl

-/

def preordToCat : Preord.{u} ⥤ Cat where
  obj X := Cat.of X.1
  map f := f.monotone.functor

  simp only [← sup_eq_right, ← hf.map_sup, h.eq_iff]

--src: Mathlib.Order.Category.FinPartOrd
theorem FinPartOrd_dual_comp_forget_to_partOrd :
    FinPartOrd.dual ⋙ forget₂ FinPartOrd PartOrd =
      forget₂ FinPartOrd PartOrd ⋙ PartOrd.dual := rfl

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Metric
@[simp]
theorem center_im (z r) : (center z r).im = z.im * Real.cosh r :=
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.Order.Category.NonemptyFinLinOrd
instance : SplitEpiCategory NonemptyFinLinOrd.{u} :=
  ⟨fun {X Y} f hf => by
    have H : ∀ y : Y, Nonempty (f ⁻¹' {y}) := by
      rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hf
      intro y
      exact Nonempty.intro ⟨(hf y).choose, (hf y).choose_spec⟩
    let φ : Y → X := fun y => (H y).some.1
    have hφ : ∀ y : Y, f (φ y) = y := fun y => (H y).some.2
    refine IsSplitEpi.mk' ⟨⟨φ, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    swap
    · ext b
      apply hφ
    · intro a b
      contrapose
      intro h
      simp only [not_le] at h ⊢
      suffices b ≤ a by
        apply lt_of_le_of_ne this
        rintro rfl
        exfalso
        simp at h
      have H : f (φ b) ≤ f (φ a) := f.monotone (le_of_lt h)
      simpa only [hφ] using H⟩

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Interval.Basic
@[to_additive (attr := simp)]
theorem bot_mul : ⊥ * t = ⊥ :=
  rfl

    OneTruncation₂ ((SSet.truncation 2).obj (nerve C)) ≃ C where
  toFun X := X.obj' 0
  invFun X := .mk₀ X
  left_inv _ := ComposableArrows.ext₀ rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl

protected lemma le_rfl : a ≤ a := a.le_refl

--src: Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Defs
@[simp] lemma mk_zero : (⟨0, le_rfl⟩ : ℝ≥0) = 0 := rfl

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Arithmetic
@[deprecated Nat.cast_ne_zero (since := "2024-10-17")]
theorem natCast_ne_zero {n : ℕ} : (n : Ordinal) ≠ 0 ↔ n ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero

--src: Mathlib.Data.Int.Defs
lemma pred_self_lt (a : ℤ) : pred a < a := by unfold pred; omega

--src: Mathlib.Data.Fin.Basic
lemma natCast_le_natCast (han : a ≤ n) (hbn : b ≤ n) : (a : Fin (n + 1)) ≤ b ↔ a ≤ b := by
  rw [← Nat.lt_succ_iff] at han hbn
  simp [le_iff_val_le_val, -val_fin_le, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt, han, hbn]

--src: Mathlib.Data.Nat.Cast.NeZero
theorem one_le {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] : 1 ≤ n := by have := NeZero.ne n; omega

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Ring.Unbundled.Rat
@[simp] lemma divInt_nonneg {a b : ℤ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) : 0 ≤ a /. b := by
  obtain rfl | hb := hb.eq_or_lt
  · simp
    rfl
  rwa [divInt_nonneg_iff_of_pos_right hb]

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic
instance instNeZeroOne : NeZero (1 : Ordinal) :=
  ⟨Ordinal.one_ne_zero⟩

--src: Mathlib.Data.Num.Lemmas
@[norm_cast]
theorem lt_to_nat {m n : Num} : (m : ℕ) < n ↔ m < n :=
  show (m : ℕ) < n ↔ cmp m n = Ordering.lt from
    match cmp m n, cmp_to_nat m n with
    | Ordering.lt, h => by simp only at h; simp [h]
    | Ordering.eq, h => by simp only at h; simp [h, lt_irrefl]
    | Ordering.gt, h => by simp [not_lt_of_gt h]

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

  ⟨fun {X Y} f hf => by
    have H : ∀ y : Y, Nonempty (f ⁻¹' {y}) := by
      rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hf
      intro y
      exact Nonempty.intro ⟨(hf y).choose, (hf y).choose_spec⟩
    let φ : Y → X := fun y => (H y).some.1
    have hφ : ∀ y : Y, f (φ y) = y := fun y => (H y).some.2

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

/-- The equivalence between `Preord` and itself induced by `OrderDual` both ways. -/
@[simps functor inverse]
def dualEquiv : Preord ≌ Preord where
  functor := dual
  inverse := dual
  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X
  counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X

@[simp]
theorem mk_eq (f : Arrow T) : Arrow.mk f.hom = f := by
  cases f
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Types
/-- The yoneda functor that sends a type to a sheaf over the category of types. -/
@[simps]
def yoneda' : Type u ⥤ Sheaf typesGrothendieckTopology (Type u) where
  obj α := ⟨yoneda.obj α, Presheaf.isSheaf_yoneda'⟩
  map f := ⟨yoneda.map f⟩

--src: Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.HomotopyCat
/-- An equivalence between the type of objects underlying a category and the type of 0-simplices in
the 2-truncated nerve. -/
@[simps]
def OneTruncation₂.nerveEquiv :
    OneTruncation₂ ((SSet.truncation 2).obj (nerve C)) ≃ C where
  toFun X := X.obj' 0
  invFun X := .mk₀ X
  left_inv _ := ComposableArrows.ext₀ rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl

  ⟨fun {X Y} f hf => by
    have H : ∀ y : Y, Nonempty (f ⁻¹' {y}) := by
      rw [epi_iff_surjective] at hf
      intro y
      exact Nonempty.intro ⟨(hf y).choose, (hf y).choose_spec⟩
    let φ : Y → X := fun y => (H y).some.1
    have hφ : ∀ y : Y, f (φ y) = y := fun y => (H y).some.2
    refine IsSplitEpi.mk' ⟨⟨φ, ?_⟩, ?_⟩

      suffices b ≤ a by

        rintro rfl

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

def dualEquiv : Preord ≌ Preord where
  functor := dual
  inverse := dual
  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X
  counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.mk <| OrderIso.dualDual X

/-- The yoneda functor that sends a type to a sheaf over the category of types. -/
@[simps]
def yoneda' : Type u ⥤ Sheaf typesGrothendieckTopology (Type u) where
  obj α := ⟨yoneda.obj α, Presheaf.isSheaf_yoneda'⟩
  map f := ⟨yoneda.map f⟩

--src: Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.HomotopyCat
/-- An equivalence between the type of objects underlying a category and the type of 0-simplices in
the 2-truncated nerve. -/
@[simps]
def OneTruncation₂.nerveEquiv :
    OneTruncation₂ ((SSet.truncation 2).obj (nerve C)) ≃ C where
  toFun X := X.obj' 0
  invFun X := .mk₀ X
  left_inv _ := ComposableArrows.ext₀ rfl
  right_inv _ := rfl

/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'

--src: Mathlib.CategoryTheory.IsConnected
/--
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.
The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
-/
theorem IsConnected.of_induct {j₀ : J}
    (h : ∀ p : Set J, j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J} (_ : j₁ ⟶ j₂), j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p) → ∀ j : J, j ∈ p) :
    IsConnected J :=
  have := Nonempty.intro j₀
  IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms fun {α} F a => by
    have w := h { j | F j = F j₀ } rfl (fun {j₁} {j₂} f => by
      change F j₁ = F j₀ ↔ F j₂ = F j₀
      simp [a f])
    intro j j'
    rw [w j, w j']

/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
lemma Identical.le : ∀ {x y}, x ≡ y → x ≤ y
  | mk _ _ _ _, mk _ _ _ _, ⟨hL, hR⟩ => le_of_forall_lf
    (fun i ↦ let ⟨_, hj⟩ := hL.1 i; lf_of_le_moveLeft hj.le)
    (fun i ↦ let ⟨_, hj⟩ := hR.2 i; lf_of_moveRight_le hj.le)

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem star_lf_zero : star ⧏ 0 := by
  rw [lf_zero]
  use default
  rintro ⟨⟩

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem lt_or_fuzzy_of_lf {x y : PGame} : x ⧏ y → x < y ∨ x ‖ y :=
  lf_iff_lt_or_fuzzy.1

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic
instance wellFoundedLT_toType_lt (o : Ordinal) : WellFoundedLT o.toType :=
  o.out.wo.toIsWellFounded

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic
instance wellFoundedLT : WellFoundedLT Ordinal :=
  ⟨lt_wf⟩

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic
protected theorem not_lt_zero (o : Ordinal) : ¬o < 0 :=
  not_lt_bot

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Ordinal.Exponential
@[simp]
theorem log_one_right (b : Ordinal) : log b 1 = 0 := by
  obtain hb | hb := lt_or_le 1 b
  · exact log_eq_zero hb
  · exact log_of_left_le_one hb 1

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
theorem identical_comm {x y} : x ≡ y ↔ y ≡ x :=
  ⟨.symm, .symm⟩

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
/-- If `x` and `y` are identical, then a left move of `x` is identical to some left move of `y`. -/
lemma Identical.moveLeft : ∀ {x y}, x ≡ y →
    ∀ i, ∃ j, x.moveLeft i ≡ y.moveLeft j
  | mk _ _ _ _, mk _ _ _ _, ⟨hl, _⟩, i => hl.1 i

--src: Mathlib.SetTheory.Game.PGame
lemma Identical.equiv {x y} (h : x ≡ y) : x ≈ y := ⟨h.le, h.ge⟩
